---
title: "05 — Select a national model with 2023 data"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** discrimination, Brier score, and overall calibration on a later year (2023), after model families were tuned on earlier historical years. Race is *not* a feature and AI/AN subgroup metrics are *not* used to choose the winner.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Fit candidate models and select winner

Fits candidate models on 2014–2022 and compares them on 2023. The Brier score measures
the mean squared error of predicted probabilities.

```{r fit-candidate-models-and-select-winner}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Candidate fitting and 2023 selection
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Fit candidates using the development checkpoint and evaluate them on 2023.
# Freeze the winner using overall weighted Brier error rather than subgroup results.

training <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_development")
selection <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_selection_2023")
tuning <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "04_tuning")

rows <- list()
families <- c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (index in seq_along(families)) {
    family <- families[index]
    parameter <- if (family == "logistic") NA_real_ else as.numeric(tuning[[family]])
    set.seed(seed + index)
    fitted <- fit_classifier(family, training, parameter)
    save_once_rds(fitted, "models", paste0("05_", family))
    probabilities <- predict_classifier(fitted, selection)
    rows[[index]] <- data.frame(
        family = family,
        parameter = if (is.na(parameter)) "default" else as.character(parameter),
        weighted_metrics(selection$FMD, probabilities, selection$RAW_WEIGHT)
    )
}

# A prevalence-only predictor is the reference for H1 (useful signal beyond baseline).
training_prevalence <- weighted_mean(training$FMD, training$train_weight)
baseline <- weighted_metrics(
    selection$FMD,
    rep(training_prevalence, nrow(selection)),
    selection$RAW_WEIGHT
)
results <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)[order(brier)]
# The results are ordered by Brier error; freeze the first family as the winner.
winner <- results$family[1]


# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(results, "05_2023_model_selection")
save_table(data.frame(family = "prevalence_only", baseline), "05_2023_baseline")

# Persist this run-specific object for downstream stages without intentionally
# overwriting an existing artifact.
save_once_rds(list(
    chosen_family = winner,
    chosen_by = "2023 survey-weighted Brier score",
    training_years = development_years,
    selection_year = selection_year,
    feature_names = feature_names,
    training_prevalence = training_prevalence
), "models", "05_frozen_selection")

print(results)
print(data.frame(family = "prevalence_only", baseline))
cat("[SELECTED] ", winner, " (2023 overall Brier score)\n", sep = "")
```


## Show model errors on 2023

Visualizes comparison to the prevalence-only reference; lower Brier score indicates
better probability prediction.

```{r show-model-errors-on-2023}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selection-year probability error
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Display candidate errors alongside the historical-prevalence reference.
# Lower Brier error indicates more accurate probabilities on this selection sample.

plot_data <- data.table::rbindlist(list(
    results[, .(family, brier)],
    data.frame(family = "prevalence_only", brier = baseline$brier)
))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data, ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(family, brier), y = brier, fill = family)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    atg_scale_fill_models() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2023 out-of-time probability prediction error",
        subtitle = "Survey-weighted Brier score, compared with baseline",
        x = "Model family",
        y = "Brier score (lower is better)"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "05_2023_brier_comparison", 8, 5)
```
